quantContext.note: From this project's own scoring pipeline (companies.json + screener.js, Phases 1-5/7), included for reference only - not itself a research source.

whyCheapBearCase.answer: LEN trades below book value (P/B 0.95) with a low P/E (13.25) [source: 1], and the filings show this is a genuine earnings-deterioration story, not just sentiment. FY2025 (fiscal year ended November 30, 2025) net earnings attributable to Lennar were $2,078 million versus $3,933 million in FY2024, a 47.2% decline, with diluted EPS falling from $14.31 to $7.98 (-44.2%) [source: 2, 6]. Even excluding one-time items (mark-to-market technology gains and a Millrose Properties exchange-offer loss), adjusted diluted EPS still fell from $13.86 to $8.06, a 41.9% decline - so this is overwhelmingly a real operating decline, not an accounting artifact [source: 2]. Management's own FY2025 10-K Outlook states plainly: 'Lennar's fourth quarter and year-end 2025 results reflect what is and continues to be a difficult housing market...our margin has been under pressure' [source: 2]. Most tellingly, management cut full-year FY2026 delivery guidance mid-year: the FY2025 10-K (filed January 2026) guided to 'approximately 85,000 homes' for full fiscal 2026, while the Q2 FY2026 10-Q (filed June 2026) revised that down to '82,000 to 83,000 homes, reflecting current pressures on interest rates and continued macro uncertainty' [source: 2, 3] - a real, quantified guidance cut during the fiscal year, not merely analyst pessimism.

revenueEpsTrend.answer: Deteriorating across every period examined. FY2025 total revenues were $34,187 million versus $35,441 million in FY2024, down 3.5% [source: 2, 4]. Q2 FY2026 (fiscal quarter ended May 31, 2026) revenue was $7,940 million versus $8,378 million in Q2 FY2025, down 5.2%; H1 FY2026 revenue was $14,559 million versus an implied $16,009 million in H1 FY2025 (derived from the 9-month FY2025 cumulative revenue of $24,819 million less the $8,810 million Q3 FY2025 quarter, both from the same XBRL series), down 9.1% [source: 4]. Earnings declined even faster than revenue: Q2 FY2026 net earnings were $305 million versus $477 million in Q2 FY2025, down 36.2%; H1 FY2026 net earnings were $534 million versus an implied $997 million in H1 FY2025, down 46.4% [source: 4]. Diluted EPS fell from $1.81 (Q2 FY2025) to $1.24 (Q2 FY2026), down 31.5%, and H1 diluted EPS fell from $3.77 to $2.17, down 42.4% [source: 4]. This is a consistent, accelerating, multi-period decline across revenue, net earnings, and EPS - not a one-quarter blip.

marginTrend.answer: Compressing, and management has explicitly guided this to continue. The Q2 FY2026 10-Q's Outlook section states expected gross margins of 'approximately 16%' for the upcoming quarter and notes 'our margin remains under pressure as we continue to focus on bringing affordable housing to an affordability-constrained consumer base' [source: 3]. This follows the same message in the FY2025 10-K Outlook: 'while our margin has been under pressure...the underlying demand is still strong, while supply is short' and 'margins will remain under pressure in the first quarter of 2026,' with Q1 FY2026 margins guided to between 15% and 16% [source: 2]. The magnitude of the net-earnings decline outpacing the revenue decline (net earnings -46.4% vs revenue -9.1% for H1 FY2026) [source: 4] is itself direct arithmetic evidence of margin compression, consistent with management's qualitative commentary about giving up price/incentives to maintain sales volume in a weak affordability environment.

guidanceChange.answer: Guidance was cut during fiscal 2026, and this is directly quotable from two filings at two points in time. In the FY2025 10-K (filed January 28, 2026), management guided: 'We expect to deliver approximately 85,000 homes in the full 2026 fiscal year' and Q1 FY2026 margins 'between 15% and 16%' [source: 2]. By the Q2 FY2026 10-Q (filed June 29, 2026), management stated: 'For the full year, we are adjusting our annual delivery guidance to 82,000 to 83,000 homes, reflecting current pressures on interest rates and continued macro uncertainty,' alongside near-term guidance for gross margins of 'approximately 16%' and SG&A of '8.8% to 9.0%' [source: 3]. This is a real, quantified, roughly 2,000-3,000 home (2-3%) reduction to full-year delivery guidance disclosed directly in the filings, not inferred from news.

catalysts.text: Active, aggressive share buyback into price weakness: Lennar repurchased shares at declining average prices through Q2 FY2026 ($92.78/share in March, $88.74 in April, $85.17 in May 2026), with $1.007 billion still authorized as of May 31, 2026 under a $5 billion program with no expiration date - buying more shares as the price fell.

Federal government attention to housing affordability: the FY2025 10-K Outlook states 'the federal government has intensified its focus on the national housing crisis, with a strong likelihood of taking decisive action to enhance affordability,' describing this as 'the first time in decades that the federal government is actively recognizing the vital role that housing plays' - a potential policy tailwind, though management itself notes 'the specifics of potential programs remain to be seen.'

Continued new community/product launches despite the downturn: Lennar debuted two new home collections (Sutton and Hollis) at its Valencia community in Santa Clarita Valley in August 2026, indicating continued active investment in new product even amid the guidance cut (per cached Yahoo headline).

risks.text: Explicit, quantified guidance cut to full-year FY2026 home deliveries (85,000 to 82,000-83,000) 'reflecting current pressures on interest rates and continued macro uncertainty' - a real, filed, in-year reduction to management's own forward expectations.

California wildfire risk is specifically and separately disclosed as a risk factor (not just general natural-disaster boilerplate): 'the incidence of large wildfires in California has substantially increased in recent years and the risk of future wildfires is expected to increase. The housing markets in areas affected by California's recent wildfires have been adversely affected by increased insurance costs and difficulties in obtaining homeowners' insurance, which was exacerbated by the January 2025 wildfires in Los Angeles.'

Analyst price-target cut: Truist Securities maintained a Hold rating on Lennar but lowered its price target to $80 (per cached Benzinga/Finnhub headline dated August 6, 2026), a real, dated, sourced signal that at least one analyst sees limited near-term upside even at the current depressed price.

verdict.reasoning: The filing evidence leans toward 'value trap' risk rather than clean 'opportunity.' Unlike EIX or ALL (where a single disclosed factor explained an otherwise-strong operating picture), Lennar's earnings decline is broad-based and ongoing: revenue, net earnings, and EPS have all fallen for multiple consecutive periods (FY2025 vs FY2024, and further in H1 FY2026 vs H1 FY2025), margin compression is explicitly guided to continue, and management itself cut its own full-year delivery guidance mid-year rather than merely facing external skepticism [source: 2, 3, 4]. The stock's low P/B (0.95) [source: 1] could reflect the market correctly pricing in a genuinely weaker housing cycle rather than an overreaction. That said, this is not a clean value trap either: management frames the underlying demand as 'strong' with supply short, the company is buying back stock aggressively at depressed prices, and there is a real (if uncertain) federal-policy tailwind around housing affordability [source: 2, 3]. Confidence is medium because the housing cycle's trajectory (further deterioration vs. a bottoming process) is genuinely uncertain from two fiscal years of filings alone, and because the guidance cut, while real, was relatively modest in magnitude (roughly 2-3% of full-year deliveries).

sourcingNote: Three of the six cached headlines were not cited: 'Lennar (LEN) Declines More Than Market: Some Information for Investors' (generic price-action commentary, no new factual content beyond what the filings already establish), 'New Homes Sit On Market For 9.3 Months As Builders Slash Prices' (industry-wide, not LEN-specific), and 'Berkshire Goes All-In on Housing Bet With Taylor Morrison Deal' (about a competitor, not Lennar) and 'Builder Mortgage Executive Karen Klemcke Joins Cornerstone Capital Bank' (unrelated personnel move) were excluded as not usefully citable.
